Example discrete-time survival data with an external registry

ExampleData_discrete.Rd

A simulated cohort whose follow-up is recorded in six intervals (for instance, years after transplant), a large external registry cohort from a related population, and the registry's published model. It illustrates the discrete-time families (discretekl(), discrete_MDTL(), discrete_indi()) and cv.bregsurv() with target_discrete().

Usage

data(ExampleData_discrete)

Format

A list with six components:

train

The internal cohort, 150 subjects: z, a data frame of covariates Z1–Z6; interval, the last interval each subject was at risk in (1–6); status, 1 when the event happened in that interval and 0 when the subject was censored at its end.

test

An independent cohort of 2,000 subjects from the same population, in the same form.

external

The registry's records, 1,000 subjects, in the same form.

beta_external

The registry's published coefficients, named Z1–Z5 (the registry did not record Z6).

Q_external

Their precision matrix (the inverse of their covariance matrix), 5 x 5.

baseline_external

The registry model's baseline cumulative-hazard increments over the six intervals.

Details

The interval hazard follows a grouped proportional-hazards model, \(h_k(z) = 1 - \exp\{-\exp(\alpha_k + z^\top\beta)\}\), with \(\beta = (0.7, -0.6, 0.5, -0.4, 0.3, 0)\) and \(\alpha_k\) rising from \(-2.6\) to \(-1.8\). Z4 is binary and the other covariates standard normal. The registry's population has effects \((0.8, -0.5, 0.6, -0.3, 0.35, 0)\) and a baseline 0.15 higher on the log scale; its published model is a grouped proportional-hazards fit to its records on Z1–Z5. Subjects are censored at the end of a uniformly drawn interval. The data are built by tools/make_ExampleData_discrete.R in the package sources.
